label: Third-person masculine (he/his) context
explanation: The feature fires on function words — mostly prepositions (of, in, with, to, by) and verbs — inside clauses referring to a man via he/his/him, never on the pronouns themselves. It is strongest when the fired-on preposition immediately precedes "his" ("in his bones", "with his wife") or a verb directly follows "he" ("he drank", "he confessed"); "he"/"He"/"him" are followed by a firing 16–22% of the time versus a 0.8% baseline. It stays silent at sequence starts and in text without an established male referent, including female-referent and impersonal passages.
